title: Check yourself: Safe retries and circuit breakers

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Scenario: Tern Payments' transfer tool writes its idempotency key to a keys table and then makes the transfer as a second, separate step. A crash falls between the two steps, and after the restart a retry returns the stored receipt although no money moved. What design prevents this?

options.text: Delete stored keys that are older than a minute, so that a retry can proceed afresh
options.says: Ruled out because the page says to "Record the key together with the effect", and deleting keys breaks the recognition of repeats.

options.text: Make the agent confirm the account balance in its prompt before every retry
options.says: Ruled out because "a control that must hold is enforced in code outside the model".

options.text: Write the transfer first and the key second, as two steps in that order
options.says: Ruled out because it only reverses the gap: "a crash between the two leaves an effect with no key, or a key with no effect".

options.text: Persist both together as one indivisible operation
options.says: The key and the effect are recorded in one step, so neither can exist without the other.

origin.section: A retry is safe only when the repeat is recognised

questions.stem: Scenario: Quillon Labs runs fifty tasks that depend on one search agent whose backend is down. Each task retries three times before failing. What limits the waste best?

options.text: A breaker that trips after repeated errors in a row and refuses calls for a pause
options.says: A breaker refuses calls at once while it is open and probes once after the cooldown.

options.text: A larger retry count for each task, so the backend has more chances to come back
options.says: Ruled out because "an unlimited retry is a way to spend money while nothing changes" and a larger count is the same mistake.

options.text: A faster model for the search agent, so that every failed call ends sooner
options.says: Ruled out because the waste is the count of calls, "a hundred and fifty wasted calls", which speed leaves in place.

options.text: A rule that restarts the whole run from the first task whenever any task has failed
options.says: Ruled out because a restart makes the same calls again, where the breaker means "the task fails fast with the reason `circuit open`".

origin.section: Retries have limits, and not every failure is a retry
